question: Assuming Gareth Evan's Generality Constraint, if I understand a proposition Fa, should I be able to understand Fx (\forall x)? Assume I understand universal quantification.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No. Evans' Generality Constraint requires recombinability among singular thoughts (if one can think Fa and Gb then one can think Fb and Ga), but a universally quantified proposition ∀x Fx has an essentially different structure—it is not itself a singular predication and does not follow merely from recombinability of singular Fa thoughts plus grasp of the quantifier. Additional resources (domain-wide semantic competence, etc.) are needed.

(The question's parenthetical “assume I understand universal quantification” removes only the quantifier-specific obstacle, not the singular-vs.-general structural gap.)

2.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes, under Evans' Generality Constraint one should be able to grasp ∀x Fx. The constraint requires that any subject who possesses the conceptual constituents of a thought (here the monadic predicate F and the singular term a) must be capable of recombining those constituents freely with other understood elements. Because universal quantification is stipulated to be already understood, the open sentence Fx is simply the result of detaching a from Fa and treating the predicate as unsaturated; the quantifier can then bind the free variable without introducing any new conceptual material. Thus the same recombinatorial capacity that lets one move from Fa to Fb (for any understood b) equally permits binding the variable to produce the universally quantified proposition. Any apparent barrier would violate the systematicity the constraint is meant to enforce.

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes, under Evans' Generality Constraint, grasping Fa already requires possessing the open predicate F and the capacity to apply it to any object in the domain one can think about. Since the constraint demands that the thought-components recombine freely, and you are also stipulated to grasp universal quantification itself, the natural extension is that you can form the thought ∀x Fx by binding the free variable in Fx with the quantifier. This recombination is precisely what the constraint enforces to ensure thoughts are structured rather than atomic.

It concerns systematic recombination of object-concepts and first-level predicates within atomic thoughts. Universal quantification ∀x Fx is not a recombination of this sort; it deploys an additional, higher-level quantificational concept whose mastery is independent of GC. Hence, even granting grasp of the quantifier, understanding Fa does not, by GC alone, yield understanding of ∀x Fx.

(The question appears to conflate GC’s intra-level recombinability with the distinct capacity to form quantified propositions.)

public_text.9: Yes, under the Generality Constraint one should be able to understand ∀x Fx once Fa is grasped and universal quantification is independently understood. Evans' requirement is that the predicate F must already function as a detachable, recombinable constituent of thought rather than being fused idiosyncratically to the singular term a. That detachability directly supplies the open predicate position Fx; the separately mastered quantifier then binds the variable without introducing any new conceptual material beyond what GC already licenses. The No arguments correctly note that GC itself does not introduce quantificational structure, but they overlook that the constraint operates precisely by guaranteeing free recombinability of any constituents the thinker already possesses—including the variable-binding apparatus once it is granted. If F could be applied only to particular singulars and not to the variable slot opened by an understood quantifier, that would constitute exactly the sort of arbitrary limitation on systematicity that the constraint rules out. The atomic-versus-quantified distinction therefore does not block the transition; it is already accommodated by treating the quantifier as one more understood element available for recombination.

Treating this step as “extra logical structure” outside GC’s reach would render the constraint’s insistence on systematicity empty precisely where generality is most explicit. The No position therefore underestimates how the stipulated quantificational competence converts GC’s recombinatory requirement into unrestricted predicate application across the domain.
